Quick answers:
- We can do either: invoice Contoso directly (Redwood invoice) or route billing through Azure Marketplace private plan. For marketplace billing we typically ask for the publisher ID and the SKUs to be set up; Azure then invoices Contoso and pays Redwood per the marketplace payout schedule.
- Co-sell: Redwood would be the listed publisher. If Contoso needs to be the reseller/co-sell partner, we will coordinate the co-sell enrollment and revenue-share in the SOW appendix.

1) Laura (our counsel) will send a redlined NDA and call out any commercial items to align on.

3) Marissa from Partner will reach out to coordinate publisher and co-sell onboarding with Azure.

Ellen —

Thanks for the SOW and procurement checklist. I've attached a redlined NDA (NDA_Redwood_Contoso_redlines.docx) and summarized the material commercial points below so we can align quickly:

Key redline points
- Indemnity and liability cap: we propose mutual indemnities and a liability cap capped at fees paid in the prior 12 months (standard for SaaS/inference vendors).
- Data handling / residency: Redwood will maintain EU/US data residency controls per the SOW appendix; any special residency requirements should be noted now.
- Audit rights: we can accept limited audit rights with reasonable notice and scope; SOC2 report can be provided under NDA.
- Payment terms: we can accept net-45, but need to confirm if any marketplace routing changes treasury timing (Azure payout schedule may differ).
- Co-sell / revenue share: commercial appendix needs to specify the split and whether Contoso will be the reseller of record or a co-sell partner for Microsoft crediting.

Action items for Contoso to confirm: preferred billing path, PO template fields (we received your template), and any specific insurance/indemnity thresholds.

I'll hold the NDA redlines and am available for a short call to go through the changes — Connor, Marissa, please confirm availability.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
